originalTitle: Australia news live: Hastie ‘not worried’ as One Nation eyes his seat and says he hopes to get their preferences
content: NSW Icac’s Operation Rosny hearings resume The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption (Icac) has resumed its hearings as part of Operation Rosny. Appearing first today is businessman Frits Maré, a key witness at a 2023 parliamentary inquiry which preceded Icac’s inquiry. At that inquiry, Maré described being asked by members of the Reformers to contribute $50,000 to an operation to unseat Alex Hawke, Liberal federal MP for Mitchell. Later today, the inquiry expects to hear from NSW shadow attorney general and Liberal leader in the upper house, Damien Tudehope. Tudehope, who has stood aside from his shadow cabinet roles during the inquiry, is not named in any allegations and is not accused of any wrongdoing. His name has been mentioned frequently during hearings so far. Reformers Jean-Claude Perrottet and Christian Ellis worked as staffers in Tudehope’s office, and Tudehope gave frequent talks at Reformers recruitment events. His son, James Tudehope, is not named in allegations but has declined a request to give evidence to Icac after moving to New Zealand earlier this year. Tudehope’s business former partner Michael O’Hara, who is alleged to have made prohibited donations, was the inquiry’s first witness. O’Hara disputed whether his payments to the Reformers counted as political donations. Matt King has described the NSW State of Origin team as the “love of his life” after being named as Laurie Daley’s permanent replacement as the new Blues head coach. AAP reports Daley walked away from the role on Monday after leading the Blues to a series victory last month and the NSWRL has wasted no time in appointing King as his replacement on Tuesday. King played nine games for the Blues and has been part of the coaching staff under Daley and Michael Maguire over the last three series. The 45-year-old King, who played for Melbourne, Souths and Warrington, has never been a senior coach but has spent the best part of the last decade working as an assistant to Trent Robinson at the Sydney Roosters. King said: I’ve had a front-row seat the last couple of years with Laurie and 12 months before that with Michael Maguire and I have a true understanding of what it means to lead this great state of ours. The one true rugby league love of my life has been the NSW Blues and to know now that I have the opportunity to guide the team moving forward, means the absolute world to me. Thomas Bradley, a Queensland supreme court judge, will be appointed Queensland’s new governor. Bradley will replace the former state chief health officer Jeannette Young, who has served in the role since 2021. He will be appointed in November. The premier, David Crisafulli, announced the decision at a press conference in the state’s defunct upper house chamber on Tuesday, flanked by his deputy premier, committed royalist Jarrod Bleijie, and Bradley. Crisafulli said Bradley had been selected in May, but the king had only approved his appointment last week. “I share the goals of my predecessors as governors of Queensland to carry out the constitutional responsibilities with dignity, fairness, and a commitment to the rule of law,” Bradley said, on Tuesday. He went on: I look forward to spending time with as many Queenslanders as possible across the state as I serve, I call to mind all that we have in common as Queenslanders, the joy that we share in each other’s successes, and the comfort that we give each other in our sorrows. I’m reminded that in communities large and small, we are part of one common endeavor. He has served on the supreme court since 2018 after a career as a legal academic and commercial barrister, and was promoted to the court of appeal in 2025. Labor reaching ‘right balance’ on gambling laws: Marles The acting prime minister, Richard Marles, says Labor’s changes to gambling advertising laws are reaching the right balance on community safety, even after a day of damning evidence in a parliamentary inquiry. Anti-gambling advocates Tim Costello and Luke Bateman told a Senate inquiry on Monday about instances where gambling companies had provided problem gamblers with drugs, sex workers and alcohol to keep them betting. Company representatives from Sportsbet and Tabcorp will give evidence today. Marles was asked about the allegations during a press conference in Sydney. “Certainly the evidence that was given tells an appalling story,” he said. “That’s that’s really clear, and I found that evidence quite shocking.” Asked if the government would go further on limiting inducements, the promotional tools used by companies to keep gamblers betting, he said Labor had already done more than any other government. We’ve looked at this issue in detail over a long period of time. There is a balance that has to be struck here, and we intend to reach that balance. But in the process, we’ve engaged in the toughest set of reforms in respect of gambling and gambling advertising that we have seen. Andrew Hastie said he’s “not worried” about the next election, but hopes he receives preferences from One Nation when it comes down to it. Hastie spoke to News24 (formerly Sky News) this morning ahead of One Nation’s expected launch in his seat of Canning in Western Australia. He had this to say: I’m not worried. Everyone who comes in this job has to have a sense of their political mortality, and if this is the end, this is the end. You do your best, and it’s up to the Australian people. We’re also a democracy. So I don’t have a problem with any political party starting a branch. Hastie maintained the Coalition had ruled out any deal with One Nation for a joint government, saying the Nationals were the “one Coalition partner” for the Liberals. But he said he still hopes One Nation preferences flow to him: We’re in a two-party preferred system. So preferences matter. chineseTitle: 澳大利亚新闻直播：一国党注视着他的座位并表示希望得到他们的偏好，哈斯蒂“并不担心”
chineseContent: 新南威尔士州反腐败独立委员会 (Icac) 已恢复听证会，作为罗斯尼行动的一部分。今天首先出庭的是商人 Frits Maré，他是廉署调查之前 2023 年议会调查的关键证人。在那次调查中，马雷描述了改革者成员要求捐款 5 万美元的行动，以推翻米切尔选区自由党联邦议员亚历克斯·霍克 (Alex Hawke)。今天晚些时候，调查预计将听取新南威尔士州影子总检察长、上议院自由党领袖达米安·图德霍普 (Damien Tudehope) 的意见。图德霍普在调查期间不再担任影子内阁职务，任何指控中都没有提到他的名字，也没有被指控犯有任何不当行为。到目前为止，他的名字在听证会上经常被提及。改革者让-克洛德·佩罗泰 (Jean-Claude Perrottet) 和克里斯蒂安·埃利斯 (Christian Ellis) 在图德霍普办公室担任职员，图德霍普经常在改革者招募活动中发表演讲。他的儿子詹姆斯·图德霍普 (James Tudehope) 的名字并未出现在指控中，但在今年早些时候搬到新西兰后，他拒绝了向 Icac 提供证据的请求。 Tudehope 的商业前合伙人迈克尔·奥哈拉 (Michael O’Hara) 是调查的第一位证人，他被指控进行违禁捐赠。奥哈拉对他向改革者的付款是否算作政治捐款提出了质疑。马特·金 (Matt King) 在被任命为劳里·戴利 (Laurie Daley) 的永久替代者，成为新任蓝军主教练后，将新南威尔士州原籍队描述为“他一生的挚爱”。据美联社报道，戴利在上个月带领蓝军取得系列赛胜利后于周一辞去了这一职务，而新南威尔士大学则在周二立即任命金为他的继任者。金为蓝军打了九场比赛，并在过去的几年里一直是戴利和迈克尔·马奎尔麾下的教练组的一员。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
